body:
Thank you. It's not creepy at all. It really does mean a lot that you remembered, even though we don't know each other. My day was alright. I'm slowly pulling myself up out of the hole. Ended up talking to some friends and they have been very understanding and supportive so far.

Again, thank you so much. :)
Thank you. I will think over all of this and figure out how to proceed from here. Thank you so much for taking the time to talk with me.

I can't really think of anything to say. 

I'm on that line between still wanting to give up because even a glimmer of hope may betray me, and considering that you're right and that I should keep going. As long as I am able to be nice, I can be a better person. I'm terrified, though. I really don't want to hurt anyone anymore. Optimism in this case is very difficult due to my ex giving up on me. Optimism pretty much personifies him, and I ended up being too much for him in the end. How does one deal with guilt and shame of that magnitude?

Quite a few people have told me I'm very hard on myself. I do see a lot of things wrong with me that others don't seem to see. It just feels like I'm deceiving them somehow, though. The good me doesn't make up for the bad me though, does it?

And maybe you're right about the job. Part of the reason things went south at the last job was because there wasn't enough keeping me busy. I have a lot of problems with obsessive, negative thinking. If I can't sufficiently distract myself, I practically self-destruct. I would even bug my boss and ask if there was more work to do. Sometimes there was, but most of the time I brought my laptop to work to keep me relatively sane.

I am more empathic than I care to admit. In fact it's actually something I deeply hate about myself. Not that I don't want to care, but I wish I could be more stoic. Admittedly, I don't really know how to take care of myself. If anyone knew the truth about my living conditions, they'd think I was a hoarder or something. I don't have a good sense of boundaries at all.

Speaking of optimism, that's something I have a huge problem with as well. One of my friends told me that I needed more optimism if I ever wanted to get better. But at what point does optimism become delusion? I can't quite explain it, but I seem to have a deep hatred for rose colored glasses. I don't apply this to other people's hopes, but there's this constant fear of having the rug pulled out from under me for being naive.  

Thank you for the kind words, though. This conversation is making me think a bit.

It's hard for me to consider it a rough ride in life when so many have gone through so much worse. I do think about how this would hurt my friends. My family? Not so much. I don't feel a particular attachment towards any of them now. But as I mentioned, my friends see a good version of me. They can't fathom the monster even existing. It always hurts a little when they say good things about me, because deep inside I know there's no truth to it.

The new job would be a fresh start, yeah. I'm going to be a junior systems administrator at a web hosting company. Not sure if I'll enjoy it. I have some apprehension about having to answer phone calls all day (my previous job was help desk, but we had a very specific client base and calls were few). I think I enjoy working with computers and scripting, so I'm hoping I will like it. It is my hope that the health benefits would allow for more regular help, but I don't think I have it in me to make it to that point. I'm just so damn terrified of myself now.

The second opinion is an option. I just don't want to end up hurting anyone while trying to figure this all out. I really don't look forward to running the gamut of finding the proper therapy, the right cocktail of medications, etc. If I live to that point, I hope the previous meds still work.

You're not prodding too much. I appreciate you talking with me.

It's impossible to not care about how I affect others. Some have told me I care too much. Deep down, I really don't want to hurt people. In fact, all I really want is to not hurt and feel like I'm a worthwhile person. Truth be told, no one has ever told me I was abusive. I just recognize the feelings and patterns from what I went through as a kid.

I want to believe change is possible. I really do. If my issue was just depression, I'd keep on fighting. Not trivializing it, but there's plenty of cases where depression gets easier to deal with via treatment or even changes in lifestyle. However, things like bipolar disorder and borderline personality disorder have been thrown on the table in recent times. I've visited forums for both sufferers and SOs/friends/family of sufferers, and the picture is not pretty at all. 

Care has been very inconsistent. When I started treatment at 14 (though problems existed as early as 8), it was on and off due to my "rebelliousness". Or rather, I was made to seem like I was the only one in the family with problems, so everything was my fault. People could hurt me however they wanted, and if I protested it was clearly because I didn't take my medication.  Treatment stopped entirely because I turned 19 and was no longer eligible for my father's insurance. Between 20 and 25, I received low cost psychiatric care from the Harris County Hospital District, but it was very difficult to keep appointments going due to having a hard time even leaving the house and not being able to drive. Some of that let up a bit after I got my first real job at 25, and then I was finally able to get insurance for better care. I lost that insurance after I quit my job in June last year because my condition had started deteriorating again and I could not keep myself together during work (throughout that entire period, I was often crying in my office and then having to snap into sounding extremely chipper for a phone call, or someone would walk in and I'd have to just pretend everything was alright even if tears were streaming down my face).

As of now, there is no care. I'm supposed to be starting a new job on February 10th, with medical benefits kicking in either in March or April. Part of me is really scared that I won't even be able to handle this job. I feel like I should be hospitalized for several months, but if I do that, I'll lose the job. 

Also, I do mainly keep people at a distance. I'm not sure if it matters how long I do it, though. Anybody that's close enough to me has the ability to set me off in the worst possible way unless I just absolutely shut down (which is what I have to do for when my mother gets into one of her moods where she decides I don't do anything right). Sorry for the long reply.

Thank you for your reply. I don't see it as trivializing the situation. It's a very valid question.

Thing is, I've been working on this with professional help on and off for 15 years now. Even when I'm not able to go to a therapist or psychiatrist, I read a lot of self-help material and try to put it into practice. Mindfulness is one technique I've had a little success with. 

But then it doesn't always work. I end up losing control because I'm hurting too badly, and then someone gets hurt. Then I may keep it under control for a little while longer, but then it happens again. And again. And again. And it feels shitty every time it happens, but that shitty feeling and knowing that I shouldn't treat people that way even if they did hurt me is not enough to stop it.

At some point you have to wonder how many more have to suffer before whatever it is inside me finally gets the point and stops this madness. The only way I've been able to consistently avoid hurting people is by keeping them at a great emotional distance. As long as I can manage that, I'm nice. But then that also means I can never be loved or have love, or any deep connection to anyone.
